summary:
ORBITAL is a browser-based space mission design game inspired by NASA’s Artemis SLS. Players design their own launch vehicle from modular parts (RS-25-style engines, fuel tanks, stage decouplers, a flight computer, a heat shield, parachutes, a satellite payload and an Orion-style capsule) and then fly the mission themselves. Built with Babylon.js, it simulates gravity, atmospheric drag, staging, re-entry heating and live orbit prediction.

It addresses the challenge by making the design itself the gameplay: every choice has a consequence. Weak thrust-to-weight stops liftoff, a missing heat shield burns the capsule on re-entry, and a satellite must reach a stable orbit above 150 km to count. A Mission Control system with XP and levels, flight-analysis charts, scoring and a leaderboard rewards smarter designs, while a scaled Solar System map invites exploration.

This matters because it turns aerospace engineering trade-offs into something anyone can learn by playing, directly in a browser with no installation, and it can inspire the next generation of space engineers.
details: ORBITAL is a browser-based 3D space mission design game inspired by NASA’s Artemis SLS, built with Babylon.js and playable in any modern browser with no installation. Players assemble their own launch vehicle from ten modular parts, including RS-25 engines, fuel tanks, stage decouplers, a flight computer, a heat shield, parachutes, a satellite payload, an aerodynamic module and an Orion-style capsule, and a pre-launch check enforces real engineering rules such as a minimum thrust-to-weight ratio of 1.15. They then launch from a detailed spaceport and fly the mission themselves. The simulation uses real constants and models gravity, an exponential atmosphere, drag, changing mass, staging, an autopilot with prograde and retrograde lock, live orbit prediction with periapsis and apoapsis markers, time warp, and re-entry heating where the heat shield ablates and the vehicle is destroyed if heat reaches 100%. Above 100 km, players can release a satellite, which counts as stable if its periapsis is above 150 km, and they can bring the capsule home with a two-stage parachute landing at 6 m/s or less. The world includes a Kennedy-inspired launch complex with a vehicle assembly building, crawler transporter and service equipment, terrain and sea, a sky that fades into stars and galaxies, Earth seen from space, and a scaled Solar System map. Five missions with XP and levels, flight-analysis charts, scoring with grades from S to D, and a local leaderboard reward smarter designs. ORBITAL matters because it turns aerospace trade-offs into something anyone can learn by playing, and it can be shared with a single web link. Visual models are simplified for gameplay, but the flight physics follow real orbital mechanics.
